answer: An identity acts only through a vertex: a machine whose silicon the knoll certifies once and then burns, so a rented fleet buys only as many identities as it owns real hosts. The knoll inscribes a voyage for each vertex, and no identity acts without its voyage. A new vertex is cut only from a core still humming in the vertex it descends from, so each clone adds a machine and its power forever: the operator's thousandth identity keeps a thousand machines humming. A fork inherits its parent's core. A lone honest agent needs one machine.
